mainTopic: Whether heirs own their father's קרבן; whether a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמן atones; whether an עולה atones for a מצות עשה skipped after הפרשה
overview: The גמרא asks whether heirs own their father's קרבן. One proof says that two heirs cannot make a תמורה because they are partners. The גמרא answers that the פסוק includes the heir but speaks of only one person. It defends this answer against a comparison to redeeming מעשר שני. רב אסי then argues that if even one heir can make a תמורה, the קרבן must atone for him, as רבי יוחנן teaches. רב אשי answers that it atones for the heirs only indirectly. Next comes a new question: does a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמן atone? רב ששת בריה דרב אידי reasons that it does not, since the owner must still bring a second one. A last question asks whether an עולה atones for a מצות עשה skipped after the animal was set aside. A proof from a ברייתא about skipping סמיכה is pushed away by רבא. רב הונא בר יהודה starts a new reading of that ברייתא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two heirs cannot substitute, so they must be partners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that heirs own the animal: that is why two heirs, like any partners, cannot make a תמורה. If they did not own it, they should be able to.
steps.simpleTranslation: And partners cannot make a substitution. But if you say the animal does not belong to the heirs, they should be able to make a substitution too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an attempted proof that heirs own their father's קרבן. It points out that if they did not own it, there would be no reason to stop them from making a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that two heirs cannot make a תמורה. If the heirs own the animal together, they are שותפין, and שותפין cannot make a תמורה, so the rule makes sense. If they do not own it, nothing should stop them, since heirs normally can make a תמורה. So the rule seems to show that the heirs do own it.

keyTerms.meaning: partners who own something together
make a תמורה, a substitution: trying to swap another animal for a קרבן
it becomes theirs, they own it
if you say

steps.confusionAlert: A תמורה does not take the holiness away from the original קרבן. Both animals end up holy. The question here is only who has the power to make one.

phrases.english: and partners cannot make a substitution.
phrases.notes: This finishes the line before it: if the heirs own the animal, they are partners.

phrases.english: But if you say
that it does not belong to them,
let them also make a substitution!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא קַנְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun before this section, about whether heirs own their father's קרבן.
steps.raayaObject: That heirs own their father's קרבן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that two heirs cannot make a תמורה, which fits only if they are שותפין.

steps.title: The verse includes the heir, but only one heir
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The doubled verb in the פסוק adds the יורש, but the verb is singular, so only one heir can make a תמורה and two cannot, whoever owns the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says 'If he shall at all change.' That comes to include the heir: one person can make a substitution, but two cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. Two heirs cannot make a תמורה because of how the פסוק is worded, not because they own the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An heir can make a תמורה only because the doubled phrase הָמֵר יָמִיר adds him. The verse speaks of one person, so its extra power reaches only a single heir. That means the rule about two heirs says nothing about ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there
'shall at all change': a doubled verb that the גמרא reads as adding something
to include, to add
heir

phrases.english: There it is different,
as the verse states:
"If he shall at all change"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:10. The verb is said twice, and that extra word is what adds the heir.

phrases.english: to include the heir;
one can make a substitution,
but two cannot make a substitution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by giving another reason for the rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that heirs own the קרבן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule against two heirs comes from the singular wording of the פסוק, not from the heirs being partners.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the singular wording of a פסוק can limit what the extra word adds.

steps.title: Then two heirs could not redeem מעשר either
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד attacks the singular-verb reading. The פסוק about redeeming מעשר also includes the יורש with a doubled singular verb. Would two heirs then be unable to redeem it, with the added fifth?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד objected: If so, by tithe, where it says 'And if he will redeem' to include the heir, should we also say one can redeem but two cannot?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד challenges the reasoning from step 2. He shows that the same reading would give a wrong result for מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק on מעשר שני uses the same pattern, גָּאֹל יִגְאַל, which also adds the יורש. By step 2's logic, only one heir would redeem with the חומש, and two heirs would not. But that is not the הלכה, since partners do add the חומש. So the singular-verb reasoning looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: he challenged it
if that is so (introduces a strange result)
tithe, here מעשר שני, which can be redeemed with money
'shall surely redeem': a doubled verb
redeems

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד:
phrases.english: Rav Ya'akov of Nehar Pekod objects to it:
If that is so,
regarding tithe, where it is written:
"And if he will redeem"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:31. Here the heir is included in having to add a fifth when he redeems.

phrases.english: to include the heir,
so too, should one redeem
but two not redeem?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a singular verb which adds the heir limits it to one heir.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading of the מעשר פסוק would exclude two heirs from redeeming with a חומש, but they are not excluded.

steps.title: מעשר is different: the father could redeem as a partner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מעשר is different. Even the father himself could redeem מעשר while owning it with a partner. So heirs, who step into his place, can redeem it as partners too. With תמורה, partners never could.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tithe is different, because with their father too, it works in a partnership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב יעקב's challenge by showing that the מעשר case is not the same as the תמורה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse adding the heir gives him the same power the father had. With מעשר, the father could redeem even as a partner, so two heirs can as well. With תמורה, partners could never make one, so the extra heir is limited to a single person. The reading from step 2 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: their father
partnership
it exists, it applies

steps.whatToRemember: Two heirs cannot make a תמורה because the פסוק that adds the heir speaks of one person. With מעשר שני, two heirs can redeem with the חומש, because even the father could redeem as a partner.

phrases.english: Tithe is different,
since with their father too
it applies in a partnership.
phrases.notes: He means the father could redeem it even when he owned it together with someone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי מַעֲשֵׂר, דְּגַבֵּי אֲבוּהוֹן נָמֵי אִיתֵיהּ בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 and keeps the reasoning of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The singular verb should limit מעשר redemption to one heir, just as with תמורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding the heir gives him the father's power. The father could redeem מעשר as a partner but could not make a תמורה as a partner.

steps.title: רב אסי: One heir can make a substitute, so heirs must own it
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי argues that the rule itself proves ownership. If one heir alone can make a תמורה, he must own the animal. Otherwise, how could even one heir do it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said to רב אשי: You can prove it from this very rule. If the heirs own the animal, it makes sense that at least one heir can make a תמורה. But if they don't own it, how can even one heir make a תמורה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי brings a new proof that heirs do own their father's קרבן. He builds it from the same rule the גמרא just discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2-4 explained why two heirs cannot make a תמורה. רב אסי turns to the other half of that rule: one heir can. Making a תמורה seems to need some ownership, so if the heir can do it, he must own the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And from this itself (the proof comes from the very rule being discussed)
It is acquired by them; they own it
To make a תמורה (to swap another animal onto the קרבן)
At least one

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַסִּי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said to Rav Ashi:
But from this itself
phrases.notes: He means the rule we just learned: two heirs can't make a תמורה, but one can.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is acquired by them,
that is why at least one can make a substitute;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָא קַנְיָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: but if you say it is not acquired by them,
how can he make a substitute?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רב אסי לרב אשי ומינה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the singular-verb reading survived, רב אסי uses the 'one heir can' half of the rule to prove ownership again.
steps.raayaObject: That heirs own their father's קרבן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that a single heir can make a תמורה

steps.title: Support from רבי יוחנן: Only the one atoned for can make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי backs up his proof with a teaching of רבי יוחנן. When someone consecrates an animal for another person, only the person it atones for can make a תמורה. So if an heir can make a תמורה, the קרבן must atone for him, and that means he owns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי אבהו say in the name of רבי יוחנן: The one who consecrated the animal adds a fifth when redeeming it. The one it atones for is the one who can make a תמורה. And someone who separates תרומה from his own produce for his friend's produce gets to choose which כהן receives it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי continues his argument by quoting רבי יוחנן. Making a תמורה belongs only to the person the קרבן atones for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן splits the owner's powers: the consecrator adds the fifth, but the one being atoned for makes the תמורה. So the power to make a תמורה depends on getting atonement. If one heir can make a תמורה, the קרבן must atone for him, which suggests the heirs acquire it.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who consecrated the animal
Adds a fifth when redeeming something הקדש
The person the קרבן brings atonement for
The person who separates תרומה
The benefit of choosing which כהן gets the gift

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abbahu say in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The one who consecrates adds a fifth,
and the one being atoned for makes a substitute,
and one who separates teruma from his own produce for his friend's produce,
the benefit of choosing is his!
phrases.notes: He is the one who picks which כהן gets the תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: והאמר רבי אבהו אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רב אסי's claim that making a תמורה needs a real connection to the קרבן.
steps.raayaObject: That an heir who can make a תמורה must be atoned for by the קרבן, and so must own it
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching that only the מתכפר makes a תמורה

steps.title: It atones for the heirs only indirectly
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the קרבן was not set aside for the heirs, so it does not atone for them directly, and they do not own it. But it does atone for them indirectly. That indirect atonement is enough to let one heir make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: By its essence it does not atone for them. Incidentally, it does atone for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רב אסי's challenge. The קרבן atones for the heirs only indirectly, so one heir can make a תמורה without the heirs owning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי assumed there were only two options: full atonement with ownership, or no atonement at all. The answer adds a middle level: indirect atonement. That is enough for one heir to make a תמורה, but it does not make the heirs owners.

keyTerms.meaning: From its essence; directly, by what it was set aside for
Incidentally; indirectly, on the side
It atones

phrases.english: By its essence, it does not atone,
phrases.notes: Meaning it does not atone for the heirs, since it was never set aside for them.

phrases.english: incidentally, it does atone.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say the heirs own the קרבן. They get some atonement on the side, which is enough for a תמורה, but the קרבן is still not theirs.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels of atonement. Direct atonement goes with owning the קרבן. Indirect atonement is enough for one heir to make a תמורה, but it does not make the heirs owners.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in steps 5-6 by adding a middle level of atonement.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that being able to make a תמורה means the heirs own the קרבן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that any atonement means ownership. Indirect atonement allows a תמורה without ownership.

steps.title: Do offerings slaughtered for the wrong purpose atone?
steps.stepSummary: A new question. The משנה taught that these קרבנות are still valid but do not count for the owner's obligation. Do they at least atone for the sin they were brought for, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Did these קרבנות atone for what they were brought for, or did they not atone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a question. This sets up a discussion that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמן does not count for the owner's obligation. Now the גמרא asks something separate: even though the obligation is not fulfilled, does the קרבן still bring atonement?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (the חכמים)
Did they atone?
For what they were brought for

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Did they atone for what they came for,
or did they not atone?

steps.whyThisMatters: This separates two ideas: fulfilling your obligation and getting atonement. The coming discussion depends on that difference.
steps.triggerLanguage: איבעיא להו כיפרו על מה שבאו או לא כיפרו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the heirs discussion and opens a new question on the משנה's main rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a קרבן slaughtered שלא לשמן still atones for the sin it was brought for, even though it does not fulfill the owner's obligation

steps.title: Logic shows the wrong-purpose קרבן does not atone
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי argues that these קרבנות do not atone. If they did, there would be no reason to bring a second קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת son of רב אידי said: It makes sense that they did not atone. If you think they did atone, why does the owner bring a second קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question from step 8. He uses simple logic to show that a קרבן slaughtered for the wrong purpose does not atone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the owner still has to bring another קרבן. If the first one had already atoned, the second one would have no job to do. So the first one must not have atoned.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
They atoned
If it enters your mind, if you would think
The second one (the replacement קרבן)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said:
It stands to reason that they did not atone;
for if it enters your mind that they did atone,
why does the second one come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a קרבן brought שלא לשמה atones.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It does not atone, because the owner must still bring a second קרבן.

steps.title: If it does not atone, why offer it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. If the first קרבן does not atone, what is the point of bringing it on the מזבח?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what then, they did not atone? Then why is it offered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's logic. It turns his question around: if the first קרבן does nothing, why bring it at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת asked why the second קרבן is needed. Now the same kind of question hits the first one. If it has no atonement value, offering it seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather what? (introduces a counter-challenge)
Is offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: But rather what, they did not atone?!
Then why is it offered?
phrases.notes: Now the question is about the first קרבן, the one slaughtered for the wrong purpose.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the wrong-purpose קרבן does not atone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it does not atone, there is no reason to offer it, just as he argued there would be no reason for the second one.

steps.title: רב אשי explains what רב ששת meant
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains: the first קרבן is offered only because of its original holiness, and the second one is what atones. But if the first one atoned, the second one would have no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is what bothered רב ששת. If you say they did not atone, that works: the wrong-purpose קרבן is offered because of the holiness it got when it was set aside for the right purpose, and the second one comes to atone. But if you say they did atone, why does the second one come?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends רב ששת by explaining his reasoning more fully. Saying the first קרבן does not atone fits everything, while saying it does atone leaves the second קרבן with no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first קרבן is offered because it was already made holy for its proper purpose, and that holiness does not go away. So it has a reason to be offered even without atoning. The second קרבן then does the atoning. Only the view that the first one atoned leaves something unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what was difficult for him
Granted, it works out well
Not for its proper purpose
On the strength of its original proper purpose
To atone

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת בריה דרב אידי, as רב אשי explains him, a קרבן slaughtered for the wrong purpose does not atone. It is still offered because of its original holiness, and the owner's second קרבן brings the atonement.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a קרבן can be offered on the מזבח because of its holiness even when it does not do its main job of atoning.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi —
phrases.notes: This is the same רב ששת from step 9, just another way of saying his name.

phrases.english: this is what was difficult for him:
Granted, if you say they did not atone,
the one slaughtered not for its sake comes on the strength of its being for its sake,
and why does the second come? To atone;
but if you say they did atone,
why does the second one come?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by clarifying the reasoning of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the original argument so that both קרבנות have a purpose.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the first קרבן does not atone, it seems to have no reason to be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is offered because of its original holiness. The second קרבן atones. Only the view that the first one atones leaves the second without a purpose.

steps.title: Does an עולה atone for a sin done after setting it aside?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if someone skipped a positive מצוה after setting aside his animal, does that animal atone for it?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages asked: For a positive מצוה violated after the animal was set aside, does it atone or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question. It asks whether a קרבן can atone for a sin committed after the animal was already designated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person sets aside an animal to atone for something he already did. Here the sin came later, after the animal was designated. The question is whether the קרבן still covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the Sages
A positive מצוה
Setting aside an animal as a קרבן
It atones

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
for a positive commandment violated after designation,
does it atone, or does it not atone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion was settled.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an עולה atones for a עשה violated after the animal was set aside.

steps.title: Side one: maybe an עולה works like a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that an עולה might work like a חטאת. A חטאת only atones for a sin done before the animal was set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say it is just like a חטאת? A חטאת atones for a sin done before the animal was set aside, but not for a sin done after. So here too, the עולה would atone for what was done before הפרשה, but not after.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out the first side of the question from Step 12, using the חטאת as a model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is set aside for one specific sin. A sin done later is simply not the sin it was set aside for. If an עולה follows the same pattern, a מצות עשה skipped after הפרשה would not be covered.

keyTerms.meaning: just like; the same as (a comparison)
sin offering, brought for one specific sin
setting aside (designating) an animal as a קרבן
before / after

phrases.english: Do we say it is just like a sin offering?
Just as a sin offering: for what was done before designation, yes,
but for what was done after designation, no.

phrases.aramaic: אַף הָכָא נָמֵי – דְּקוֹדֶם הַפְרָשָׁה אִין,
phrases.english: So too here: for what was done before designation, yes,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the עולה, which atones for skipped מצות עשה.

phrases.english: but for what was done after designation, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first side of the question asked in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should an עולה be treated like a חטאת, and only atone for what came before הפרשה?

steps.title: Side two: maybe an עולה is different from a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe an עולה is not like a חטאת. One עולה covers many skipped מצות עשה at once, so it might also cover one skipped after הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is not like a חטאת. For a חטאת, you need a separate חטאת for each sin. But here, since one עולה atones for several מצות עשה together, it should also atone for a מצות עשה skipped after the animal was set aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. It argues that an עולה works differently from a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is tied to one sin, so a later sin cannot be included. An עולה is not tied to one sin. It covers a whole group of skipped מצות עשה, so there may be no reason to cut off ones that came after הפרשה. The question is now fully set up, and the גמרא will look for a proof.

it is not similar

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא – כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא כַּמָּה עֲשֵׂה גַּבֵּיהּ מְכַפְּרָא,
phrases.english: But here, since it atones even when there are several positive מצוות with it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question begun in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Since an עולה covers many מצות עשה together, does it also cover ones skipped after הפרשה?

steps.title: A ברייתא about skipping סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. If someone treats סמיכה as an unimportant extra and skips it, the פסוק views it as if he did not get atonement, yet he did get atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "He shall lean... and it will be accepted." Does leaning (סמיכה) atone? Atonement only comes through the blood, as the פסוק says, "For the blood atones for the soul." So why does the פסוק say "lean... accepted... to atone"? To teach that if he treated סמיכה as a leftover, unimportant part of the מצוה, the פסוק views it as if he did not get atonement. Yet he did get atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. In this step it only quotes the ברייתא; the next step will show how it answers the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק links סמיכה to atonement, when only the blood atones. It answers that skipping סמיכה leaves the person "as if" not atoned, even though the קרבן still worked. That odd phrase, "as if he did not atone, and he did atone," is what the גמרא will use as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: leaning one's hands on the head of the קרבן
atonement
a leftover, non-essential part of a מצוה
the פסוק views him as if

steps.confusionAlert: "As if he did not atone, and he did atone" is not a contradiction. The קרבן really did atone, but the פסוק treats him as if something is still missing.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And he shall lean... and it shall be accepted"
Does leaning hands atone?!
Isn't atonement only through the blood,
as it says: "For it is the blood that atones for the soul"!
So what does the verse come to teach with:
"And he shall lean... and it shall be accepted... to atone"?
That if he treated leaning as a leftover part of the מצוה,
phrases.notes: He saw it as an optional extra, so he skipped it.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ לֹא כִּיפֵּר,
phrases.english: the verse views him as if he did not get atonement,
and yet he did get atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to settle the two-sided question of Steps 13 and 14.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an עולה atones for a מצות עשה skipped after הפרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 1:4 about someone who skipped סמיכה.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא: no atonement for the skipped סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא this way. "He did atone" refers to מצות עשה skipped before הפרשה. "He did not atone" refers to the skipped סמיכה, which is a מצות עשה skipped after הפרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't "he did atone" mean for a מצות עשה skipped before the animal was set aside? And "he did not atone" means for the מצות עשה of סמיכה, which was skipped after the animal was set aside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof from the ברייתא. It suggests the ברייתא shows an עולה does not atone for a מצות עשה skipped after הפרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סמיכה can only be skipped once there is an animal set aside, so skipping it is always an "after הפרשה" failure. If the ברייתא says he is not atoned for that, then an עולה does not cover מצות עשה skipped after הפרשה, just like a חטאת. The phrase "מאי לאו" (doesn't it mean...?) presents this as the likely reading, but it is still open to being pushed back.

keyTerms.meaning: doesn't it mean...? (suggests a reading as proof)
it atoned
which counts as

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading makes side one (Step 13) the stronger side: an עולה would work like a חטאת and only atone for what came before הפרשה.

phrases.english: Doesn't "he did atone" mean
for a positive מצוה skipped before designation,
and "he did not atone" means for the positive מצוה of leaning,
which counts as a positive מצוה skipped after designation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא from Step 15 in a way that answers the question from Steps 13 and 14.
steps.raayaObject: An עולה does not atone for a מצות עשה skipped after הפרשה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's phrase "as if he did not atone, and he did atone," split between before and after הפרשה.

steps.title: רבא: the case of סמיכה does not answer our question
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof from סמיכה. The obligation of סמיכה stays open until שחיטה, so it is only missed after שחיטה. That is a case we never asked about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You bring a proof from the מצות עשה of סמיכה? That case is different. As long as he has not slaughtered the animal, he still stands under the command to place his hands on it. When does he actually fail to do the מצוה? Only after שחיטה. And about after שחיטה, we never had a question.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the proof from step 16. He says the case of סמיכה does not fit our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our question was about a מצוה skipped after הפרשה but before the animal is brought. With סמיכה, nothing is lost before שחיטה, because he can still do it. The מצוה is only truly missed after שחיטה. Everyone agrees an עולה would not cover a sin from after שחיטה, so the ברייתא tells us nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing one's hands on the head of a קרבן before it is slaughtered
"It is different there." A standard way to show a proof does not match our case.
Slaughtering the animal
"Stand and place your hands." He is still obligated and able to do it.
"We do not have a question about it." The point is already obvious.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying סמיכה is not a real מצוה. His point is only about timing. Skipping סמיכה only becomes final after שחיטה, which is outside the case we asked about.

phrases.english: Rava said: You are citing the positive מצוה of placing hands?!
It is different there,
since as long as he has not slaughtered,
he stands under "stand and place hands";
phrases.notes: In other words, he can still go ahead and do סמיכה, so nothing has been missed yet.

phrases.english: When does it become a skipped positive מצוה?
After the slaughter;

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן.
phrases.english: and about after the slaughter, we have no question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in steps 15-16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא about סמיכה, as explained in step 16
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Skipping סמיכה is only final after שחיטה. Our question is about the time between הפרשה and שחיטה, so the case does not match.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof did not hold up, so the question from step 12 is open again. In step 18, רב הונא בר יהודה begins a new reading of the ברייתא, and his reading continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב הונא בר יהודה starts a new reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה suggests a different meaning for "he atoned." It means the person got atonement. The second half of his reading comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said to רבא: Say instead that "he atoned" means the person was atoned for.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה begins a new way to read the ברייתא's two phrases, "he atoned" and "he did not atone." This step sets up his full reading, which continues right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 read the two phrases as two different sins, one skipped before הפרשה and one after. רב הונא בר יהודה offers another option: "he atoned" refers to the person himself. If that works, the ברייתא no longer has to be about before and after הפרשה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: "Say." Introduces another way to read a source.
He atoned; the offering brought atonement
The man; the person himself
